subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The 1939 Futurama Vision
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The 1939 Futurama Vision.

hook.text: At the 1939 World's Fair, General Motors showed visitors a highway full of cars with no drivers.

buildup.text: The Futurama exhibit imagined a 1960s America where automated highways guided cars magnetically.

discovery.text: Millions of visitors lined up to see the future—then walked outside to roads full of horse carts.

twist.text: GM's prediction was off by about 80 years, but the core dream of driverless cars never faded.

climax.text: That single exhibit planted the self-driving idea in the public imagination for the rest of the century.

punchline.text: A theme park ride in 1939 predicted the cars of 2025.

quiz.question: Where was the Futurama self-driving car exhibit displayed?

details.summary: General Motors' Futurama exhibit at the 1939 World's Fair depicted a future highway system with automated cars guided by radio signals, planting the first seeds of the autonomous vehicle dream in public imagination.
details.whyItMatters: Futurama shaped decades of thinking about automated transportation. The vision of cars driving themselves on smart highways inspired researchers and continues to echo in modern autonomous vehicle concepts.
takeaways: GM's exhibit imagined automated highways in the year 1960
Over 5 million visitors experienced the Futurama ride
The concept of vehicle-highway cooperation persists in V2X technology

faq.question: How accurate was the 1939 Futurama prediction?
faq.answer: Futurama correctly predicted wide multilane highways and suburban sprawl. Its automated driving prediction was decades too optimistic, but the concept of vehicle-to-infrastructure communication is now being developed as V2X technology.

faq.question: Did Futurama directly influence autonomous vehicle research?
faq.answer: Yes. Researchers in the 1950s through 1970s explicitly cited Futurama when proposing automated highway systems. The idea of embedding guidance technology in roads influenced infrastructure-based approaches to autonomy.
